summary: Encapsulation keeps an object's data behind methods so the object can reject bad values. Python uses an underscore name plus @property to do this.
notes: _gpa is private by convention only. Python still lets outside code read and write it.
@property and @gpa.setter must use the same method name, gpa.
self.gpa = gpa in __init__ uses the setter, so a bad starting GPA is rejected too.
pitfall: Naming the stored field gpa instead of _gpa makes the setter call itself forever and causes RecursionError: maximum recursion depth exceeded.
